clue.text: Tiny Tom's elated by sign of approval

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the English folk tale, so his surname with the possessive gives these letters
someone elated is up, in high spirits

explanation.surface: A little boy called Tom is thrilled by a gesture of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb, the thumb-sized boy of English folklore, is the 'Tiny Tom'; his possessive surname supplies the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised thumb is the familiar gesture of approval, so the phrase names that signal.

clue.text: Lady and lord follow a state official

indicators.note: in this down clue the abbreviation for lord comes after the letter a, following it

parts.note: a lady is referred to as her

explanation.surface: A woman and a nobleman trail behind a government functionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follow' applies only to the lord: he comes after 'a', and the lady stays at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald was an officer of state who made royal proclamations and kept rolls of arms.

clue.text: Is engrossed by French word for "dewy"

indicators.note: something engrossed by another is absorbed into it, so the word is goes inside

parts.note: mot is the French for word

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the French term is for the adjective dewy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a French translation of 'dewy'; really 'French word' is just a container, and 'dewy' is the English definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewy grass is covered in fine droplets, so it is slightly wet.

clue.text: Woman and daughter in warehouse on the docks

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a dock labourer rather than a noun, read as the one working on the docks

indicators.note: the woman and daughter are placed inside the warehouse word

parts.note: a store is a warehouse
Eve, the first woman, is the crossword's stock female name

explanation.surface: A mother and her daughter are found in a dockside warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the loose 'on the docks', meaning the person who works there; 'in' puts the woman and daughter inside the warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads cargo ships, so this worker spends the day at the quayside.

clue.text: Opposition supporter put on trial

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another sits above it, so pro comes first

parts.note: a pro is someone in favour, a supporter
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A political opponent's backer is placed on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposition' looks like the parliamentary party, but it is the definition in the sense of objection.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest is an expression of objection, so it amounts to opposition.

clue.text: Represent one Catholic in admin. Unit

indicators.note: one and Catholic are placed inside the administrative unit

parts.note: a department, abbreviated DEPT, is a unit of administration
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single Catholic stands for a section of the civil service.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray something in a picture or words is to represent it.

clue.text: Imagine having drive and energy in the morning!

parts.note: DR is the street-name abbreviation for drive
E is the physics symbol for energy
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: A cheerful exhortation to picture being full of drive and energy at breakfast time.
explanation.definitionFit: To fantasise about something is to picture it in the mind, i.e. to imagine it.

clue.text: That poses problems very quickly

indicators.note: the letters of these words pose problems and must be rearranged into new order

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that this creates difficulties, and fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problems' is the anagram signal working on THAT POSES; 'poses' is part of the fodder, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with the utmost speed and urgency is acting very quickly.

clue.text: HP terms available in Devon

definitions.note: a locating phrase standing for a place found in that county

parts.note: hire purchase (HP), the British instalment plan, is a form of credit
something available is on, as in on offer

explanation.surface: Hire-purchase deals are on offer in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: HP is hire purchase, the British term for buying on instalments. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crediton is a market town in mid Devon, north-west of Exeter.

clue.text: Rockery plant or coniferous shrub

parts.note: a pine is a cone-bearing evergreen

explanation.surface: A gardener choosing between an alpine plant and a small conifer.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpine is a succulent sedum, a stonecrop often grown in rock gardens.

clue.text: Exceed the mark to prove set wrong

indicators.note: the letters of these words are set wrong, put into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone goes too far in trying to show a group to be mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To go beyond a limit is to overstep it, as in overstepping one's authority.

clue.text: Entire corps of sappers on the qui vive

parts.note: all means entire, the whole
the RE, Royal Engineers, is the British Army corps of sappers, giving the article plus RE

explanation.surface: A whole regiment of military engineers is alert.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; the corps is 'the RE', the Royal Engineers, so the article is included.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert and quick-witted, fully in possession of one's faculties, is being mentally sharp.

clue.text: Material broadcast by medical boss

parts.note: MOH is the Medical Officer of Health, the head of local public health
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Fabric promoted on radio by the senior doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests a homophone, but it means AIR; the MOH was the British local Medical Officer of Health.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is a fabric or yarn made from the hair of the Angora goat.

clue.text: Usually found in 50 per cent of cases

definitions.text: Usually found in 50 per cent of cases

parts.words: Usually found in 50 per cent of cases
parts.note: something happening in half of all instances happens with even odds, which is what this everyday phrase for usually says literally

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase literally means 'with equal frequency as not', i.e. half the time, yet it is used to mean 'usually'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means frequently or more often than not, while literally describing even odds.

clue.text: Temperate seamen can gain points on time

parts.note: ABs are able seamen
a tin is a can
E and N are points of the compass

explanation.surface: Moderate sailors manage to get extra credit for punctuality.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who abstains from alcohol is moderate in habits, so self-restrained.

clue.text: Secure records are vital for manicurists

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for tools a manicurist cannot do without

parts.note: to nail something is to fasten or secure it
files are records

explanation.surface: Keeping safe the records is essential for a beauty salon.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: the things that are essential tools for those who do manicures.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery boards and metal rasps for shaping fingertips are the basic tools of a manicure.

clue.text: Cite rave review for showing originality

indicators.note: to review is to look over again, so these letters are revised into a new order

explanation.surface: A critic quotes a glowing write-up praising a fresh approach.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inventive and imaginative is showing originality.

clue.text: Interrogate six coarse men afresh

indicators.note: the letters of these words are arranged afresh, in a new order

explanation.surface: Six rough men are questioned all over again.
explanation.definitionFit: To question a witness closely, especially one called by the other side in court, is to interrogate.

clue.text: Friend based in America for a short term

indicators.note: the friend is based inside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: a crony is a close friend

explanation.surface: A pal living in the USA for a brief period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short term' reads as a brief period of time, but means an abbreviated word.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed from initials, like NATO, is an abbreviated expression.

clue.text: Deserter captured by soldiers is not charged

indicators.note: the deserter ends up inside, captured by the soldiers

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is someone who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: A runaway caught by troops is let off without any charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not charged' suggests a legal release; it means free of cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given free costs nothing, so the recipient is not charged.

clue.text: A Verdi composition full of diversity

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are recomposed

explanation.surface: A Verdi opera is praised for its wide range.
explanation.definitionFit: Something diverse has many different kinds in it, i.e. a mixed assortment.

clue.text: Object when odd newsman gets a rise

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise means the letters read upwards, so the whole charade is turned round

parts.note: rum means odd or strange
ED, editor, is the crossword newsman

explanation.surface: A complaint arises when a strange journalist receives a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets a rise' reverses RUMED upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise doubts or objections is to demur, a verb sense of object.

clue.text: Plant about to impose penalty on railway

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a fine is a penalty

explanation.surface: A factory is about to have a sanction slapped on a rail line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'soon going to'; 'about' gives RE and 'to impose... on' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A refinery is an industrial installation, and plant means industrial premises.

clue.text: Into obscene verse? Certainly not!

indicators.note: the answer lies into the words, contained within them

explanation.surface: Someone indignantly refuses to get involved with dirty poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic refusal, at no time at all, is the same as certainly not.

clue.text: Sporting official who writes verse

explanation.surface: A match official who is also a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: a man of lines, someone who writes verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or tennis official watching the touchlines; also, jokingly, a person who produces poetic lines.

clue.text: Conscript without it displays lack of gravity

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the conscript word goes round it

parts.note: to levy troops is to conscript them

explanation.surface: A draftee who lacks it shows a frivolous attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but has its old sense 'outside', so the conscript word wraps round 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Levity is frivolity, a want of seriousness.

clue.text: Nobleman carries small weight of metal ware

indicators.note: the nobleman carries the weight within himself

parts.note: a peer is a nobleman
WT is the short form, a small version, of weight

explanation.surface: An aristocrat lugging a light metal object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small weight' is the abbreviation WT, not a little weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Pewter is a tin alloy used for tankards and plates, so household goods made of metal.

clue.text: Security services emphasise her didactic skills

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the woman who has teaching skills

parts.note: MI, as in MI5 and MI6, the British military intelligence services
to stress is to emphasise

explanation.surface: Intelligence agencies highlight a woman's teaching abilities.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the woman whose skills are teaching, a schoolmistress.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistress is a female schoolteacher, one employed for her teaching ability.
